I am an old man now, 63 years, and I have farmed this land in Ruvuma for many years. This small plot near the house, only a tenth of a hectare, I plant maize together with beans like my father taught me — the beans help the soil and feed the family. I do not have money for chemical fertilizer this season, and the rains here in the south are usually enough so I do not irrigate. My sons and their wives help me with the work, so I rarely need to pay anyone from outside, though during weeding I sometimes call a neighbor for a day or two.
